title: Design System: bmiest design language v2

designLanguage.scopeNote: This file holds only what is shared. Each product keeps its own DESIGN.md with [family] and [product] tags; this file wins when they disagree. A part becomes [family] once two products ship it.

changeLog.change: Below the hero: variant B 'per guild' + variant A's edge-to-edge ticker. Removed the per-boss table, phone boss cards and current-boss cards (rcard) from the race site; added Per guild, reworked Voortgang, folded Hall of fame, one drawn disclosure chevron; board label wraps with the raiding badge on it.
Family record rewritten from four shipped products; replaces the race copy.
Family record rewritten from four shipped products; replaces the race copy.

jade.purpose: The brand and what is selected, active or OK: bug mark and day blocks, the active block of any flush switch, a selected pick's outline and subline, the primary button, the ticker label and top edge, section-head caps, the kill check, links, the disclosure chevron, the CE marker, focus rings.

jade-deep.purpose: A quieter jade for finish lines and season ends that should not read as live (race CE and season-end lines, the wishlist's viewed history row and default meter fill).

jade-ghost.purpose: Link underlines and text selection only.

gold.purpose: Earned, and nothing else: race leader, first kill and winner; a new best; the wishlist's single best upgrade; Cutting Edge and a first Dutch kill on bmiest.be.

live-red.purpose: On air, and nothing else: the LIVE block, the primary while the channel is live, a live ring on a head tile, an 'n live' block. Paper on it 4.6:1. A ground or a ring, never small text on ink.
live-red.definedIn: overlay css/tokens.css (byte copy in every product)

rose.purpose: Failed, error or stale: a failed run block (ink-900 text), an error panel's 1px border, a staleness warning. Never red.

ink-900.purpose: Page ground, the bug's name block, the ticker band, inactive switch blocks, ink text on jade, gold and class colours.

ink-850.purpose: Wells, cells, tile bodies, drop panels.

ink-800.purpose: Ribbon and pick bodies, panels, strip values.

ink-750.purpose: Pills, loot rows, strip keys, boss-head tiles, a selected pick's body, popovers.

ink-700.purpose: 1px borders, rules, chart grids, hairlines, meter tracks on dense rows.

ink-600.purpose: The 1px slanted outline of ribbons and picks, loot-row hover, dashed empty states.

ink-400.purpose: Initials on boss heads, a pick's outline on hover, the popover trigger's dotted underline.

ink-300.purpose: Secondary meta, axis labels, inactive switch text, hints.

ink-200.purpose: Pill text, strip keys, table heads, timestamps.

track.purpose: The unfilled part of a meter or race track, paper at 8%. Not in tokens.css; the wishlist defines --track, the race uses rgba(255,255,255,.09) inline.

void-glow.purpose: Hero atmosphere behind boss art only; 24% overlay, 32% race hero, 28% bmiest.be and an earned Hall of fame stage. Web only.

hero-dusk.purpose: Start of the dusk-to-teal-to-ink linear behind a full hero. Web only.

hero-deep-teal.purpose: Middle of the hero linear. Web only.

display.purpose: Once per page, uppercase, balanced; the second half may be jade. Products set their own size (88px race hero, 112px 'BMIEST').

headline.purpose: Section heads and entry titles, uppercase, behind a 14px slanted jade cap.

headline-sub.purpose: One step down, behind an 11px cap.

lead.purpose: One line under a display, max 34-40ch, paper-dim; 17px on phones.

pick-name.purpose: Names in a pick list; 15-16px on phones.

ribbon.purpose: Names on ribbons; 16px on dense lists, 14px under 400px.

body.purpose: Copy and ticker items; 14px on phones.

bug.purpose: The bug's blocks, uppercase; LIVE at 13px/.14em; 12-13px on phones.

label.purpose: Pills, switch blocks, strip keys, table heads, nav heads; uppercase.

numeric.purpose: Every number read as a value or compared; products add larger steps (race board 32px).

shadows.name: one-float
shadows.purpose: The One Float Rule: only the popover that floats over content it doesn't belong to (race kill-rank popover).

outlines.name: live-head-ring
outlines.purpose: A live stream's head tile in a pick.

outlines.name: owner-outline
outlines.purpose: Marks a guild's cell or an earned item; an outline, not elevation.

outlines.name: empty-state
outlines.purpose: Empty states only; every other border is solid.

shapes.name: slant-2
shapes.purpose: Hairline marks: a race track under a ribbon.

shapes.name: slant-5
shapes.purpose: Section-head cap, tags, lane race-track segments, footer mark.

shapes.name: slant-6
shapes.purpose: Pills, meters, bars, 40-52px boss heads, raid-frame cells, step numbers, the to-top block.

shapes.name: slant-8
shapes.purpose: Strip values, the play block, a boss tag's last block.

shapes.name: slant-10
shapes.purpose: Inner bodies: ribbon key blocks, guild blocks, pick head tiles, caption plates.

shapes.name: slant-12
shapes.purpose: Buttons: the primary and loot rows.

shapes.name: slant-22
shapes.purpose: Frames: screenshot frames, specimen panels, the rcard notch.

shapes.name: outline-construction
shapes.value: outer slanted clip 1px larger than the inner (padding:1px on the outline colour)

shapes.name: disclose-chevron
shapes.value: 7px box, 2px jade right+bottom border, rotate(-45deg) closed / rotate(45deg) open
shapes.purpose: The one disclosure mark for every <details>.

heroGround.value: radial-gradient(60% 70% at 74% 42%, rgba(63,217,164,.22), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(50% 60% at 96% 8%, rgba(150,90,255,.32), transparent 70%), linear-gradient(160deg, #1b1030 0%, #0d1a1c 55%, var(--ink-900) 100%)
heroGround.source: race hero; void strength is per-product tuning (24/28/32%), not a rule
heroGround.note: Only behind boss art. The overlay's stream pages carry no gradients (The Bitrate Rule).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Anything that travels: stage wipe, track run, row slide, card arrival. Used by race and bmiest.be; not yet in tokens.css.

motion.name: ticker-run
motion.value: translateX(-50%) linear infinite over --tk-run (about 58px/s from content length)
motion.purpose: Kills ticker; pauses on hover/focus; static scrollable row under reduced motion.

motion.name: row-slide
motion.purpose: Swapped rows slide once when the data moves.

motion.name: stage-wipe
motion.purpose: bmiest.be stage wipe; race news card 420ms.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Gutters 16px, sections 32px apart, bug and switches 34px (720-900px per product).

breakpoints.name: stage
breakpoints.purpose: bmiest.be: one entry on the stage from here up.

breakpoints.name: hero-art-band
breakpoints.purpose: Race: at or below, boss art becomes a band above the title.

bossArt.source: self-hosted alpha cut-outs trimmed to the body by the race site's boss-cutouts script, provenance embedded (impeccable embed-prompt), mapped in bossart.js; other products keep a trimmed copy of the map
bossArt.pair: a council shows both bodies unless one is under 40% of its partner's height
bossArt.mask: feet fade: linear-gradient(#000 78-82%, transparent); nothing drawn on the art
bossArt.headCrop: object-position: 50% 0 on boss heads and pick head tiles

fonts.tokens: tokens.css: colours, families, radii, spacing, motion; byte copy between products; loads no fonts
fonts.selfHosted: fonts.css: Outfit 300-800 + JetBrains Mono 400-700, latin + latin-ext woff2, SIL OFL (race #65); others still @import Google Fonts from tokens.css
fonts.holy: #ffffff exists in tokens.css for the overlay's v1 stream pages only

components.name: Broadcast Bug
components.description: [family] Flush square 40px blocks in a fixed order: LIVE (only when a fresh check says live), mark (bmiest products only), name, slot, day. Source: bmiest.be css/site.css .bug.
components.html: LivebmiestKelderklasse · EU-DraenorDag 47

components.name: Flush Switch and Tabs
components.description: [family] The language switch one step smaller for views and periods: 32px flush blocks, 12px/800 caps, real tablist semantics; the wishlist's 40px variant sits in a 1px ink-700 frame. Source: race style.css .seg, wishlist .tabs.

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Loot Row
components.description: [family] The secondary action: an ink-750 chip at the primary's height and slant, loot type in paper, 18px jade drawn icon; hover ink-600 with jade text. Source: bmiest.be .drop.

components.name: Pills
components.description: [family] Slanted ink-750 chips in label type: jade for a positive marker, gold with a star only for something earned, ink-300 neutral; a pill can be a button. Source: bmiest.be/race .pill, race/wishlist .pill--action.

components.name: Race Track
components.description: [family] Progress as a boss health bar: a slanted segment per boss, 3px apart, filled in the owner's colour from --p minus each segment's --i; the finish segment's track is jade at 20%. Nameplate size (7px, 2px slant) and lane size (14px, 5px slant). Source: race splash.css .row__hp. Snippet sets --p/--i in CSS; the product sets --p with style.setProperty().

narrative.overview:
The language of a raiding streamer's broadcast, carried onto every page the family runs. It started as the stream overlay and grew into a poster on the race site; everything since speaks it. The grammar comes from the broadcast and from the game: a **broadcast bug** of flush square blocks crowns every page, an **edge-to-edge ticker** closes the first view, standings are **ribbons** like a raid's nameplates, progress is a **health bar cut into one segment per boss**, and the art is **the boss itself**, cut out and standing in a jade and void glow with nothing drawn on it.

Everything sits on flat near-black ink: no rounded cards, no drop shadows, no glass. Shape comes from one cut, the **slant on the trailing edge** of every ribbon, pill, button, bar, chip and tile. Colour is scarce and always means something: jade is the brand and what is selected or OK, gold is earned, red is on air, rose is failed or stale, and guilds and classes bring their own colours as game data. The pages are loud at the top and dense, honest data below, where the marks explain themselves.

Each product is a different room in the same house: the overlay is the broadcast, bmiest.be is the Adventure Guide that opens onto the tools, the wishlist is the operator's raid-night sheet, and Race to Dutch First is the raid poster for the Dutch community, sharing the language but not the brand.

Confirmed rejections (direction history 2026-10-03, and since): the generic dark data dashboard ("too generic, AI-looking"), a sports-broadcast theme laid on top ("still a dashboard, not WoW"), a link-in-bio column, and a hero over a project-card grid. More gamer-like is welcome; a dashboard is not.
keyCharacteristics: Flat ink ramp, Outfit + JetBrains Mono, jade + gold, from one tokens.css copied byte for byte.
The right-edge slant on a named scale; square corners everywhere else; the bug, switches, strips and ticker are flush square blocks.
Colour as meaning: jade = brand, selected, OK; gold = earned; live-red = on air; rose = failed or stale; guild and class colours = game data.
The work shown running: live data with an honest timestamp, real renders and real screenshots, never a mock-up of itself.
Motion only when the data moves.
Every string in Dutch and English; game names never translated.

rules.name: The Gold Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Gold marks something earned: a leader, a first, a winner, a new best, the best upgrade. A tag, a hover, a progress state, a late note or a project label is never gold, and something that doesn't count earns no gold (a raid outside the race gets a grey pill).

rules.name: The Red Means On Air Rule
rules.body: Broadcast red appears only while a channel is really live, from a fresh check, and every red mark goes when it isn't. Raiding itself is jade; a failure is rose.

rules.name: The Owner's Colour Rule
rules.body: A guild's or class's colour marks that guild or class and nothing else; a guild's best effort is drawn in its own colour.

rules.name: The Quiet Timestamp Rule
rules.body: The update line says when the data was fetched ("Bijgewerkt om 13:42"), in quiet grey, never the next run and never coloured. Only data that is older than its source promises (a failed fetch, a stale Raider.IO profile) turns rose, and then with words that say so.

rules.name: The Poster Voice Rule
rules.body: Display and headlines are Outfit 800 uppercase with tight tracking. Only the bug, buttons, switch blocks, strip keys and a few rank and count blocks share that weight.

rules.name: The Mono Number Rule
rules.body: A number a visitor compares or reads as a value (kills, ranks, pulls, dates, percentages, ilvl, countdowns) is JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Raider's Numbers Rule
rules.body: State is said the way raiders say it: kills out of the counted bosses and what was left of the current boss after the best pull ("6/8 · nog 69,8%"), never a fractional position ("6,3"). Fractions only drive drawings (track fill, line height).

rules.name: The No Caption Rule
rules.body: A section carries no caption explaining what is visible; the marks explain themselves (a key with the real marks, a sort chevron, "bij alle N kills" in place). Replaces the earlier One-Line Caption Rule (race, 2026-10-06).

rules.name: The Flat Ink Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by tone and 1px lines, never by shadow or blur.

rules.name: The One Float Rule
rules.body: The single exception: a popover that floats over content it doesn't belong to (the race's kill-rank popover) casts one shadow, `0 8px 20px -6px rgba(0,0,0,.7)`, on ink-750 with a 1px ink-500 border and a caret. Panels that open under the bar (the Streamers panel) stay flat.

rules.name: The One Slant Rule
rules.body: Slants go down and to the right, on the trailing edge only. A slanted element never also gets rounded corners.

rules.name: The Data Moves It Rule
rules.body: A page doesn't move on load; it moves when the data does, once. A track runs from its old to its new position, swapped rows slide (FLIP, 650ms), only the new stretch of a line draws, a new kill lights in the ticker, a new boss crossfades in. Constant motion is limited to the LIVE dot and the ticker.

rules.name: The Along the Slant Rule
rules.body: Things that enter travel along the family slant: a wipe's leading edge leans down and to the right (bmiest.be's stage wipe, 620ms; the race news card, 420ms).

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion` only colour cues remain: the ticker becomes a static scrollable row, swaps happen without travel, counts land at their final value.

rules.name: The Bitrate Rule
rules.body: On stream pages (overlay OBS sources): no gradients, no animation across the full width, no pure white; canvas 2560×1440.

dos: Do take colours, fonts, spacing and motion from tokens.css variables; keep tokens.css a byte copy.
Do keep gold for what is earned, jade for brand and selection, red for on air, rose for failed or stale.
Do pick slants from the scale and keep the bug, switches, strips and ticker flush and square.
Do show the work running: live values with a quiet fetch time, real renders, real screenshots, specimens drawn from the tokens.
Do let every live block fall back to static content when its fetch fails.
Do move only when the data moves, along the slant, with `--ease-out`.
Do draw marks as SVG in one stroke family, in the meaning colour.
Do let a label wrap rather than cut a number off.
Do ship every string in Dutch and English; game names are never translated.
Do keep the CSP on the web products: script-src 'self', no inline styles; set custom properties with `style.setProperty()`; build DOM from external names without `innerHTML`.
donts: Don't add drop shadows, rounded cards, blur or glass (the one popover excepted).
Don't put a coloured side stripe on cards, cells or rows (a raid-frame foot bar is not a side stripe).
Don't use text glyphs (★, ✓, ▸, emoji) as icons or disclosure marks.
Don't use gold for tags, hover, progress, lateness or project labels.
Don't show LIVE, a live dot or any red unless a fresh check says live.
Don't colour the update time; say staleness in words, in rose.
Don't explain a section in a caption.
Don't add bmiest branding to Race to Dutch First, or show the person behind bmiest anywhere.
Don't build any of it as a generic dark dashboard.
